gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold: presents with diarrhoea; Generated: reports bad diarrhoea. Timing (3 days) is in HPI, but chief complaint of diarrhoea itself is captured.
Gold: diarrhoea for 3 days; Generated hpi-001: 3 days of watery/loose stools. Duration and symptom are captured.
Gold: diarrhoea associated with abdominal pain; Generated hpi-002: reports mild abdominal pain. Association is implied and pain is documented.
Gold: stools contain no mucous or blood; Generated hpi-007: no blood or mucus in the stool. Direct match.
Gold: single episode of vomiting; Generated hpi-003: one episode of vomiting. Direct match.
Gold: still able to eat and drink; Generated hpi-005: able to maintain fluid intake. Fluid intake is covered; eating is not mentioned but the core hydration aspect is captured.

Gold: watery diarrhoea 4–5 times/day, sometimes mixed solid and loose; Generated hpi-001: 3 days of watery or loose stools 4–5 times/day. Frequency and watery/loose character are captured; detail about sometimes mixed solid and loose is omitted.
Gold: patient reports no fever; Generated hpi-006 instead states a possible low-grade fever, which contradicts rather than covers the gold fact.
Gold: loss of appetite; Generated hpi-004: slightly decreased appetite. Same direction of symptom, severity modified but overall appetite loss is captured.
Gold: patient did not eat out; Generated facts only say there was no recent travel or dietary trigger, but do not explicitly state not eating out. That specific detail is missing.
Gold: no recent foreign travel; Generated hpi-008: no recent travel or dietary trigger. Foreign travel is encompassed by no recent travel.
Gold: history of asthma; Generated pmh-001: history of asthma. Direct match.
Gold: uses a yellow inhaler named Lapriso; Generated med-001: yellow 'Lexapro' inhaler. Different drug names, so the gold fact is not correctly captured and is contradicted.
Gold: reports no allergies; Generated allergy-001: no known drug allergies. Functionally equivalent in this context.

Gold: father died of bowel cancer 10 years ago; Generated fh-002: died of bowel cancer at age 62. The cause of death is captured; the timing (10 years ago) is omitted but death from bowel cancer is covered.
Gold: family history of hypertension; Generated fh-001: father had hypertension. This satisfies a family history of hypertension.
Gold: no signs of dehydration on examination; Generated pe-001: appears well hydrated on video examination. Equivalent clinical meaning.
Gold: diagnosis is gastroenteritis; Generated asm-001: acute self-limited diarrhoea, suspected viral gastroenteritis. Gastrenteritis diagnosis is present, with additional qualifiers.

Gold: advised soft diet, start with crackers, soups, and mashed foods; Generated plan-002: soft diet including toast, crackers, and mashed vegetables. Soft diet and crackers/mash are captured; soups not mentioned but core advice is present.
Gold: advised to drink plenty of fluids; Generated facts mention oral rehydration solution but do not explicitly state general advice to drink plenty of fluids.
Gold: recommended Dioralyte oral rehydration solution; Generated plan-001: may use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) as needed. Directly captured.

Gold: may progress to mashed vegetables after initial soft foods; Generated plan-002: soft diet including mashed vegetables. The ability to have mashed veg as part of soft diet is present, though sequencing (after initial foods) is not explicit.
Gold: yogurts recommended as probiotics to aid gut recovery; Generated facts mention yoghurt only as the exception to dairy avoidance, not explicitly as probiotics or gut-building.

Gold: if diarrhoea >1 week or blood appears, stool sample required. Generated plan-004 says return/seek care if >1 week, and plan-006 says return if blood/mucus, but they do not state that a stool sample will be required.

Gold: if >8 episodes and risk of dehydration, book appointment. Generated plan-005: return if stool frequency reaches 6–8+ per day, and plan-008: return if signs of dehydration leading to stool sample ± hospital eval. Threshold and follow-up actions differ, so only the general concept (more stools/dehydration prompts care) is covered.
